source.publication: 2025 MI-1040 Forms and Instructions (includes Form 4884 instructions)
source.section: Schedule 1 line 25 (PDF page 17: older of you or your spouse born 1946-1952 and reached 67; 40,000 joint); Worksheet 2 lines 1-7a (PDF page 18); PDF pages 22-23 questions 1-6; Worksheet 3.3 (PDF page 25); MI-1040 lines 9a, 10, 13-17 (PDF page 10 Line 9a, Line 10, Line 17; PDF page 11 example: line 14 income subject to tax less line 15 exemptions = line 16 taxable income)

worked: Federal AGI = spouse 2 wages 30,000.00 + interest 20,000.00 + dividends 10,000.00 + spouse 1 IRA 8,000.00 + taxable Social Security 34,000.00 = 102,000.00. Federal taxable income = 102,000.00 - federal standard deduction (31,500 + 2 x 1,600 age 65 or older = 34,700.00) = 67,300.00; given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Michigan: older spouse born 1948 (past 67), so the return takes Tier 2 (the younger spouse, born 1955, would alone be Tier 3, reduced by taxable Social Security to 40,000 - 34,000 - exemptions = 0). Line 14 Social Security 34,000.00. Worksheet 2: line 1 40,000.00; lines 2, 4, 5 0.00; line 7 40,000.00, less than the 68,000.00 of wages, interest, dividends and IRA, so Tier 2 = 40,000.00 on line 25. Worksheet 3.3 would give only the IRA, 8,000.00, so Tier 2 is more beneficial. Subtractions 74,000.00. Line 14 = 102,000.00 - 74,000.00 = 28,000.00; exemptions 11,600.00; line 16 = 16,400.00. MI-1040 line 17 tax = 16,400.00 x 0.0425 = 697.00. No credits; state income tax 697.00.
